utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-72-I, the Prosecutor versus Milan Babic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Registrar. First of all, good morning to everyone in this courtroom and also to those who are assisting us just outside this courtroom. Mr. Babic, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Babic. May I have the appearances for the Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For the Prosecution, Ms. Bauer, Ms. Walpita, and my name is Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, madam. For the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUELLER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Mr. Robert Fogelnest, co-counsel, Mr. Danilo Cirkovic, case manager, and Peter Michael Mueller.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yesterday we have heard a guilty plea on Count 1 entered by Mr. Babic, and the Chamber has taken a short while to consider that guilty plea. We have considered whether the guilty plea has been made voluntarily, whether the guilty plea was informed, whether the guilty plea was not equivocal, whether there was a sufficient factual basis for the crime and the participation of you, Mr. Babic, in that crime. This Chamber accepts your plea. It is a plea entered on Count 1 only, but on the basis of the plea agreement the Chamber expects the Prosecution now the plea has been accepted to withdraw Counts 2 and following. Could you confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The Prosecution withdraws the other counts in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, we'll deal with that in a more formal way in the days to come, but the Chamber gives its consent to the withdrawal of the other counts. That means that only Count 1 remains at this moment on which the Chamber will decide. And may I invite you, Mr. Babic, to stand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, this Chamber finds you guilty on Count 1 of the indictment issued on the 6th of November, 2003, persecutions on political, racial, and religious grounds, a crime against humanity punishable under Articles 5(h) and 7(1) of the Statute of this Tribunal. The Chamber adds to it that this crime was within the objective of the joint criminal enterprise of which you were a co-perpetrator. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The next steps to take is to instruct the registrar to set a day for sentencing. The registrar will do so after having consulted the Chamber. A provisional schedule for that has already been discussed. I do understand that the parties would agree on a sentencing hearing on the 1st and 2nd of April and the filing of sentencing briefs on the 22nd, if I'm not mistaken, of March. I'd just like to seek confirmation by the parties that two days for a sentencing hearing would be sufficient. The 1st and the 2nd of April is a Thursday and a Friday, and the Chamber would avoid to have to adjourn on Friday in the afternoon and to continue Monday morning. So, therefore, I'd like to hear from the parties how much time they would need for the sentencing hearing and the presentation of the evidence they would like to present at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the Prosecution -- the Defence and the Prosecution have actually identified two joint witnesses and -- which is one for the witness -- the victim's impact and the other one is actually the investigator who dealt with Mr. Babic. These are the two witnesses that we have identified. The Prosecution would not present any more witnesses. We would file a few 92 bis witnesses from the crime base.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: That's all. So these two witnesses, it's hard to estimate it right now, but I think it would only take about one session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One session for the witnesses. Of course, 92 bis, would there be any request for cross-examination for these 92 bis statements?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUELLER
utterances.text: I don't think so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUELLER
utterances.text: I don't think so, Your Honour. May I add to that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUELLER
utterances.text: I find myself in a very difficult position to predict how much time we would like to have and we would need. But let's -- let me say it the other way around. I would think that we should not exceed two sessions as envisaged by this time schedule. And if you are satisfied with that message, then I would appreciate it for the time being, because I'm really not ready yet to tell you precisely what we envisage. And my personal idea is that it cannot be excluded that we have to approach Prosecution again and say there is a witness which we would like to present to the Tribunal, and in case of we try to do that, perhaps as a joint witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That means that for the time being there's no necessity to schedule for more than two days. And as the parties have been aware of in this case, that sometimes if needed a scheduling order can be changed or amended. But then I'd like to hear from the party who wishes to take more time to give notice well in advance so that the new scheduling order could be issued. Yes, Mr. Mueller.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUELLER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Of course we will stick with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUELLER
utterances.text: And it's a matter of self-understanding that as far as we know something, we will communicate that to the Tribunal, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Is there any other issue at this moment that the parties would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just want to mention that we had actually this morning filed a joint motion with the materials that you requested yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And that's all. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has received copies of that material, although not with the formal confirmation of filing, but orally we were informed that they were filed. And it would -- oh, I see now that there's the confirmation of the filing as well. But under the present circumstances, the Chamber looked into the materials. We have perhaps not read every single letter of it, but we got an impression. And when we asked to present this material, it was already in the back of our minds that it might well serve for sentencing as well. Any other issue to be raised?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUELLER
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We then stay adjourned and in due course a scheduling order, presumably for the 1st and the 2nd of April, will be issued.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.03 p.m.
